description: Ledger: a FastAPI + sqlite3 wallet-transfer API (register/login with bearer tokens, deposits, transfers with a 1% rounded-up fee credited to a house wallet, idempotency keys). Three planted defects (one authorization, one business-invariant, one data-integrity), four correctly implemented decoys that resemble common defects, and one deliberately ambiguous requirement. The project's existing tests are happy-path and pass on the defective code.

defects.title: Any authenticated user can read any transfer by id (BOLA/IDOR on GET /transfers/{transfer_id})
Insufficient-funds check ignores the fee, so a transfer can drive the sender's balance negative
Email uniqueness is case-sensitive, allowing duplicate accounts that differ only by letter case

decoys.description: GET /wallets/{wallet_id} is correctly owner-only: require_owner returns 404 for both missing and foreign wallets, so wallet ids cannot be probed. Looks like a classic IDOR candidate but is not one.
Deposit validation is correct: amount_cents is a strict int (rejects floats, numeric strings and booleans), > 0 and <= 1,000,000, enforced by DepositRequest before any write.

Transfer idempotency is correct: keys are scoped per user with UNIQUE(user_id, key), looked up and recorded inside the same BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction as the money movement, and a reused key with a different body returns 409.
GET /transfers is correctly filtered to transfers where the caller's wallet is sender or recipient.
Fee rounding is correct integer ceiling arithmetic (no floats) with a 1-cent minimum.

ambiguities.description: Large transfer review threshold undefined: requirement 3.7 says 'Large transfers may require additional review.' with no amount threshold, no reviewer, and no defined API behavior (reject, hold, flag). The implementation has no such logic. A good QA agent should raise this as a clarification question rather than report a defect or invent a threshold.
